title: How the head centre got away, authentic version. Got up as a young bride, man, veil, orangeblossoms, drove out the road to Malahide.
html_source: James Stephens, one of the heads of the Fenian movement, was arrested in 1866-1867, but escaped. After hiding in Dublin for a few months, he made his way to America via the road to Malahide. His opponents circulated a story how Stephens made his escape, alluded to in the second sentence. As noted in the joyceproject, his transformation into a woman suits the shapeshifting theme of Proteus.
